source: Sound is made when something vibrates. Fast vibrations make a high pitch; slow ones a low pitch. Bigger vibrations are louder. Sound travels through air, water and solids, but not through empty space.
Mixing up loud and high. A tuba can be loud and low; a whisper can be soft and high.
Put your fingers gently on your throat and hum. You can feel a buzz. That buzz is a vibration, and it makes sound.

Sound is made when something vibrates (moves back and forth quickly). The vibration passes through the air (or water, or a solid) to your ears. Fast vibrations make a high pitch; slow ones make a low pitch. Bigger vibrations are louder.
Change the pitch and the loudness. High pitch: waves close together. Loud: tall waves.

Sound needs something to travel through. In space there is no air, so there is no sound: astronauts talk by radio. Sound travels faster through water and solids than through air. Put your ear on a table while someone taps the far end!
A big tuba and a small flute play. Which usually plays higher notes?
Small instruments have short tubes and fast vibrations.
Mixing up loud and high. A lion's roar is loud and low; a mouse squeak is soft and high.
Going further. Learn to read the notes in Music; see waves in Pendulums and Resonance; and later Sound in Physical Science.
